newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai copper futures end mixed in thin trade.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai copper futures end mixed in thin trade.

text.p: Shanghai copper futures ended mixed in thin trading on Monday due to poor fundamentals and selling pressure from big producers despite gains on the London Metal Exchange (LME) on Friday, traders said.
The most actively traded September 1997 contract ended at 23,670 ($2855) yuan per tonne, up 30 yuan from Friday's close.
The June contract fell 10 yuan to 22,970, while July shed 10 to 23,250. August rose 10 to 23,480, though October fell 20 to 23,700 and November added 100 to 23,800.
Combined volume fell sharply to 25,760 tonnes from 58,550.
Traders said an oversupply of copper on the spot market weakened market sentiment and dampened investor interest in building long positions.
Big producers were seen shorting the market with prices close to the 24,000-yuan level, which resulted in local prices moving in the opposite direction of the LME, they said.
"The LME gains did not encourage local buyers due to poor domestic fundamentals," said one trader. "The shrinking volume indicated speculative funds retreating from the market."
Some traders said they expected the market to consolidate around current levels the rest of this week as no quick reversal of the oversupply in the spot copper market is expected.
The price of physical copper is around 23,100 yuan per tonne in the Shanghai area, they said.
But other traders said they believed a further strong performance of the LME would encourage local investors to build long positions.
Aluminium ended down across the board. The June 1997 contract lost 300 to 15,000 yuan per tonne.
The July aluminium contract was untraded, while August fell 170 yuan to 15,520, September lost 420 to 15,530 and October was unchanged at 15,500.
Combined volume rose to 650 tonnes from 280 tonnes.
